headline: Open Access Along the Alaska Highway
reservation: Kluane Lake is bordered by public lands and small communities with no central entry fee; however, campsites at Destruction Bay or Congdon Creek require local payment. Verify site availability through Yukon Parks, especially during peak migration seasons.

days.title: Lakeshore Vistas and Tachal Dhal

stops.name: Tachal Dhal Visitor Centre
stops.detail: Use the mounted telescopes to spot Dall sheep on the slopes of Sheep Mountain above the lake's northern tip.

stops.name: Soldier's Summit
stops.detail: Hike the historic trail where the Alaska Highway was officially opened, offering expansive views of the Slims River delta.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour from Haines Junction; watch for frost heaves on the highway.
days.note: High winds often whip up glacial dust in the Slims River valley, reducing visibility.

days.title: Bays, Boats, and Burwash Landing

stops.name: Burwash Landing
stops.detail: Visit the Kluane Museum of Natural History to see world-class wildlife exhibits and local First Nations art.

stops.name: Destruction Bay
stops.detail: Walk the rocky shoreline of the Yukon's largest lake to see the scale of the Ruby Range mountains.

days.driving: Local driving between communities is short, but road repairs are common.
days.note: The lake is exceptionally cold; shore-based activities are safer than swimming.

days.title: Silver City and Southern Shores

stops.name: Silver City Ghost Town
stops.detail: Explore the remains of this historic mining and trading post located at the south end of the lake.

stops.name: Congdon Creek
stops.detail: Enjoy a final look at the lake from the popular shoreline camping area known for its wildflower displays.

days.driving: Allow 3-4 hours if returning to Whitehorse directly.
days.note: Check highway reports for 'pilot car' sections which can add significant travel time.

intel.title: Highway Fuel Stops
intel.text: Destruction Bay and Haines Junction are the only reliable fuel points. Never pass a station when below half a tank in this remote corridor.

intel.title: Satellite Pockets
intel.text: Expect total loss of signal between the major community hubs. Download navigation data for the Alaska Highway stretch before departing Whitehorse.

intel.title: Highway Pullouts
intel.text: Dozens of scenic pullouts line the lake. Ensure your vehicle is fully off the white line to avoid heavy transport truck traffic.

intel.title: Dust and Debris
intel.text: The Slims River area is prone to significant dust storms from the dry glacial silt. Close windows and slow down if visibility drops.

intel.title: Sheep Viewing Seasons
intel.text: Dall sheep are most visible on the lower slopes near Tachal Dhal in spring and late autumn. Summer sightings often require binoculars.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle in Whitehorse; verify the spare tire and jack are present before driving the Alaska Highway north.
plan.vehicle: Suitable for all vehicles, but RVs should be wary of narrow shoulders and gravel breaks near Destruction Bay.
plan.goldenHour: Soldier's Summit provides an elevated westward view for watching the light fade over the Saint Elias Mountains.
